transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just keep losing chunks of time every day. I work on computers, so I end up constantly re-reading emails and texts, or reopening folders I just closed. And then, before I can even leave the house or actually start my work, I find myself mentally replaying conversations over and over. It's... well, it's like I'm trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake somewhere. It's just getting really hard to manage.
Do you feel driven to mentally replay these conversations to prevent something bad from happening, or do you worry that something bad will happen if you don’t get them ‘right’ in your mind?

Well, like I was saying a minute ago, it's really about trying to prove to myself that I didn't make a serious mistake. I don't know if I'm picturing a specific disaster happening, it's just... I have to be absolutely sure I didn't mess up somewhere. 

So I get stuck. I end up losing all that time just going back over things—re-reading the same emails, reopening the work folders I just looked at, or running those conversations through my head again and again before I can even leave the house. I just can't seem to move on until I feel sure I didn't do something wrong.
Are these conversations you replay in your mind things that you don’t really want to think about, but they keep coming up and bothering you, even when you try not to focus on them?

Yes, exactly. I really don't want to be thinking about them. I'll be right in the middle of trying to work through a system design, or maybe preparing a lesson, and... well, this thought just keeps barging in. 

It'll be something like worrying I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I mishandled some family photos, or even that I let someone in the community down somehow. I try to push it away because I know I’ve already been over it, but... I just can’t seem to let it pass. It just keeps coming up and interrupting me until I focus on it again.
Do you feel that you have to perform these mental reviews or behaviors in a certain way, or a certain number of times, to feel that everything is okay or to prevent something bad from happening?

No, not really. I don't have a specific number of times I have to do it, like counting or anything. And I don't think I do it in a particular way, either. 

It's... well, it's really just about doing it until I feel sure. I just keep re-reading the email or replaying the conversation until that nagging feeling of doubt finally goes away, however long that takes. But it's not a set number or a specific routine.
Do you feel anxious or upset if you’re not able to go back and check or replay these things in your mind?

Yes, absolutely. If I try to stop myself from checking an email again, or if I'm in a situation where I can't just sit and think through a conversation, the anxiety gets pretty intense. It's like this tight, uncomfortable feeling that just builds and builds. I get really agitated because my brain is telling me I need to figure it out right that second, and if I can't, it's almost impossible to focus on anything else.
Do you ever have thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that feel intrusive and unwanted, and that you try to get rid of or neutralize in some way?

Yeah, that's... that's basically what I was trying to describe earlier. It's exactly like that. I'll be focused on something else, like working through a system design or getting a lesson ready, and the thought just barges in out of nowhere. 

They are definitely unwanted. It's usually those same worries I mentioned—that I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I somehow mishandled those family photos, or let someone in the community down. I try my best to push the thought away and just move on, because logically I know I've already been over it. But I just can't seem to let it pass. It feels completely intrusive.

Do you feel that you have to repeat certain thoughts or mental acts, like going over conversations or re-reading messages, in order to neutralize or prevent some feared event or to reduce your anxiety?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Honestly, that's the main reason I came in to see you. I keep losing these big chunks of time to it. Before I can leave the house or even start my work for the day, I get stuck re-reading emails and texts, or reopening folders on my computer just to check things. 

I have to mentally replay those conversations over and over. It's like... I'm just trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake. And doing all that repetition is the only way to get the anxiety to drop enough for me to actually get on with my day.

Do you feel driven to perform these mental reviews in a specific, ritualized way, such as needing to remember every detail perfectly or only moving on after you've reviewed the conversation 'just right' in your mind?

No, not really in a specific way like that. I don't have a set routine or a rule about how I review things. I just... I just go over it until I feel satisfied that I didn't mess up. It's not about doing it perfectly or in a certain order, it's just about getting that relief from the worry. Once I feel like I've checked it enough to know it's okay, I can stop.

Do you ever find yourself mentally replaying conversations or re-reading messages not just to ease your worry, but because you feel you have to do it in order to make things 'balanced' or 'complete' in some way, even if you’re not anxious about it?

No, it's never about making things feel balanced or complete. I don't really get that feeling. It's strictly about the anxiety. If I'm not worried about making a mistake or offending someone, I don't feel any need to go back and check things or replay conversations. It's only when that specific fear pops up that I have to do it.
